text: When you build REST APIs, clear design is essential. Start by choosing simple, meaningful endpoints that represent your resources, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct HTTP status codes so clients understand what happened; for example, use 200 for success, 404 when something is missing, and 500 for server errors. Good documentation is just as important, because it helps other developers use your API without confusion. Finally, plan for versioning from the beginning. Adding a version like /v1/ to your endpoints lets you improve the API later without breaking existing applications. Following these practices makes your API easier to use, maintain, and grow.
